# @zakkster/lite-filter

Zero-dependency, zero-GC approximate-membership filter FAMILY for JavaScript under
one uniform LiteFilter<K> surface. COMPLETE at v1.0.0: 7 members. v0.1.0 ships the
substrate + the reference member: Bloom (Bloom, CACM 1970) -- the differential oracle and
the honest floor the rest of the family improves on, one member per release. v0.2.0 adds
CountingBloom (deletable); v0.3.0 adds BlockedBloom (one 512-bit cache-line block per key);
v0.4.0 adds Cuckoo (deletable, fingerprint-based, fail-closed at capacity); v0.5.0 adds
Quotient (deletable, mergeable + resizable, fail-closed at the 0.90 load ceiling); v0.6.0
adds XorFilter (the FIRST static member -- built once from a known key set, immutable,
~1.23x space-optimal at ~9.85 bits/item, fail-closed on an unpeelable set); v1.0.0 adds
BinaryFuse (the 7th and FINAL member -- static like XOR but SMALLER: ~1.13x, ~9.04 bits/item
at n=1e6, and faster to build; Graf & Lemire 2022) and FREEZES the API (status
building -> stable). Every mutable member exposes the SAME
add/mightContain/has/size/count/capacity/fpp/clear API, so the filter is a one-line
constructor swap; the static XorFilter and BinaryFuse share the query surface but are built
via <Member>.from(keys) and throw on add/remove/clear. Single-file ESM, zero runtime
dependencies, node:test only. Ships a runnable + importable bench (Bench.mjs) that measures
ACTUAL vs THEORETICAL false-positive rate on your own keys, checked against a real Set oracle.

## Status: 1.1.0 - fail-closed option doors + string-edge entropy fix + litefilter/3 snapshots. Family complete and API frozen since 1.0.0 - Bloom (reference) + CountingBloom (deletable) + BlockedBloom (cache-local) + Cuckoo (fingerprint) + Quotient (mergeable/resizable) + XorFilter (static, space-optimal) + BinaryFuse (static, smallest).

The problem it solves: "have I seen this key?" -- dedup, set membership, cache
admission -- at a handful of BITS per entry instead of the tens of bytes a Set costs
per key, with a small, bounded, tunable false-positive rate and ZERO false
negatives, at fixed preallocated memory with no per-op allocation.

The family is the identity from v0.1.0, exactly as @zakkster/lite-lru puts its
eviction policies under one LiteCache<K,V> surface: Bloom is the reference member +
differential oracle + honest floor, and the shipped bench is the differentiator --
it measures the divergence between the textbook FPR formula and your filter's
behavior on your keys, instead of copying a number from a paper.

## The surface (LiteFilter<K>)

- add(key) -> void: record a key. Zero allocation on keys:'int' and string paths;
  arbitrary keys are amortized where they must String()-encode.
- mightContain(key) -> boolean: the query. NO false negatives -- an added key ALWAYS
  reads true. A true on a never-added key is a false POSITIVE, bounded by the
  configured fpp. One-sided: false positives only.
- has(key): the SOLE alias of mightContain (same one-sided semantics). No third name.
- remove(key): member-specific. Bloom and BlockedBloom are ADD-ONLY -- they throw a
  [lite-filter] Error (fail closed; clearing bits would cause false negatives for other
  keys). CountingBloom, Cuckoo and Quotient implement a REAL remove(key) -> boolean (return
  false and mutate nothing if the key is absent). Quotient also ships merge() + resize().
- size / count -> number: the number of adds recorded (a plain counter, not an
  estimate, not a distinct-key count -- Bloom cannot detect a duplicate add).
- capacity -> number: the item count the filter was sized for at construction.
- fpp() -> number: the CONFIGURED target while empty, else the fill-derived
  closed-form ESTIMATE (1 - e^(-k*n/m))^k. A formula, NOT a measurement -- measure
  your own keys with the bench.
- clear() -> void: reset to empty; allocates nothing (zeroes the store in place,
  same ArrayBuffer identity).

Cross-cutting, mirrored from lite-lru:
- keys:'int' strict-zero-alloc mode: 32-bit signed integer keys, mixed directly with
  no string encoding. Out-of-range / non-integer keys throw a [lite-filter] TypeError.
- Opt-in stats { stats: true }: a per-instance holder { adds, queries, hits, misses };
  OFF by default so the hot path writes nothing (_stats === null). stats()/resetStats()
  fail closed on a non-stats instance.
- dump() / static Member.restore(snap, opts?): the typed-array store IS the serial
  form, emitted as a plain array that round-trips through structuredClone and JSON;
  restore rejects any tag/member/width/capacity/fpp/seed/store-length mismatch or
  corruption (REJECT, never truncate). Bloom emits { bits }; CountingBloom emits
  { w:4, cnts } and validates every byte 0..255 (so every nibble 0..15) before build;
  BlockedBloom emits { bb:512, nb, bits }; Cuckoo emits { fw, b:4, nb, fp } (fw is the
  fingerprint width -- f is the format tag) and validates every slot 0..fpMask before build;
  XorFilter emits { fw, bl, fp } and re-derives fw from fpp, bl from count, fp.length == 3*bl,
  and every slot 0..(1<<fw)-1 before build (REJECT, never truncate); BinaryFuse emits
  { fw, sl, sc, fp } and RE-DERIVES the whole segment geometry from count (rejecting an
  internally-inconsistent sl/sc/fp.length triple), fw from fpp, fp.length == (sc+2)*sl, and
  every slot 0..(1<<fw)-1 before build.
  SNAPSHOT FORMAT v3 (litefilter/3, decisions/0021, 0023): every dump() also carries a 32-bit
  integrity checksum `chk` over the tag, mem, keys-mode, seed, every sizing/width field,
  count, and every store word. restore() recomputes it (after the tag check and the structural
  checks, before any write) and REJECTS a mismatch fail-closed. This closes a real fail-OPEN:
  keys-mode and seed cannot be re-derived from the stored bytes, so a flipped keys ("int" <->
  null) or seed used to silently reconstruct under the wrong hash path (1990/2000 false
  negatives). `chk` is an INTEGRITY check against accidental corruption, NOT a MAC (a forger who
  recomputes chk is out of scope). The tag advanced litefilter/2 -> litefilter/3 in 1.1.0
  (decisions/0023): the XOR/Binary Fuse STRING-key second hash `g` changed from fmix32(h ^ seed2)
  to an independent hashStr(s, seed2), so a litefilter/2 XOR/BF snapshot would read every string
  key FALSE. One tag is ONE algorithm for the WHOLE family, so every member is re-tagged --
  including Bloom and int-mode filters whose bytes are unchanged. A litefilter/2 (or earlier)
  snapshot is REJECTED with a migration message: re-dump() under 1.1.0 to produce litefilter/3.

## Members

- Bloom (decisions/0001): one bit array of m bits, k hash positions per key. add sets
  k bits; mightContain returns true only if all k bits are set. Add-only, one-sided,
  the textbook baseline and the differential oracle. Good for: a simple, well-understood
  membership filter at a fixed target fpp. Not for: deletes (add-only), or the
  smallest possible space at very low fpp (the static members will win there).
- CountingBloom (decisions/0007..0011): each bit becomes a 4-bit SATURATING counter,
  two packed per byte (one Uint8Array). add increments, remove decrements,
  mightContain is true iff every probed counter is nonzero. Costs ~4x Bloom's space
  and buys a REAL remove(key) -> boolean. Same FPR formula as Bloom. Two honest
  caveats: (1) removing a NEVER-ADDED key can corrupt other keys and cause a later
  false negative -- only remove keys you added; (2) a counter that SATURATES at 15 is
  clamped forever (never wraps on add, never decrements on remove), so its keys stick
  present. Good for: membership + deletes with Bloom semantics. Not for: the lowest
  space per deletable item (Cuckoo), or a multiplicity readout (deferred,
  decisions/0010 -- saturation makes it an over-estimate).
- BlockedBloom (decisions/0012..0013): the bit array is partitioned into fixed 512-bit
  BLOCKS (16 x 32-bit words = 64 bytes, one cache line). Every key is routed to ONE
  block (from its first base hash) and all k bits live inside it (odd-stride within-block
  walk), so a query touches ONE cache line regardless of k -- the throughput win. Same
  1x store size as Bloom. Add-only like Bloom: remove() throws. THE honest price: the
  block partition loses cross-block independence, so the MEASURED false-positive rate
  runs OVER the plain-Bloom formula for the same bits/item (e.g. ~0.014 vs ~0.010 on a
  uniform int workload). fpp() reports the plain closed-form as a labeled FLOOR (not a
  prediction); the bench prints Bloom vs BlockedBloom side by side (query ns down, FPR
  up). No "same fpp for free" claim. Good for: maximum query throughput where a higher
  measured FPR is acceptable (or bought back with a lower configured fpp). Not for: the
  tightest FPR at a given bits/item (plain Bloom is lower), or deletes (CountingBloom).
- Cuckoo (decisions/0014..0015): stores a small NONZERO fingerprint per key in one of TWO
  candidate buckets of b=4 slots (partial-key cuckoo hashing). i1 = hash(key) & (nb-1);
  fp = nonzero fingerprint(key); i2 = (i1 XOR hash(fp)) & (nb-1) -- an INVOLUTION, so an
  evicted fingerprint recovers its alt bucket from the fingerprint alone. add scans i1
  then i2 for an empty slot; on a full pair it KICKS a random victim to its alt bucket up
  to 500 times using a SINGLE scalar victim register (no scratch array). It DELETES via a
  real remove(key) -> boolean. Fingerprint width f = ceil(log2(8/fpp)) byte-aligned UP to
  an 8-bit (f<=8) or 16-bit (9..16) store; f>16 (fpp < 8/65536 ~ 0.000122) throws at
  construction. The FPR is width-quantized to ~2b/2^f (independent of fill), typically
  BELOW the configured target because f rounds up (at fpp 0.01, f=10 -> 16-bit -> ~0.0078);
  fpp() reports that quantized rate once non-empty. Two honest fail-closed edges: (1) add
  on a full table (500 kicks exhausted) THROWS a [lite-filter] Error -- never a silent drop
  (decisions/0014); headroom is observable via size vs capacity; (2) removing a
  NEVER-INSERTED key whose fingerprint collides with a real key removes that other key's
  fingerprint -> a false negative for it (decisions/0015) -- only remove keys you inserted.
  Space ~2x Bloom at fpp 0.01 (byte-aligned slots). Good for: membership + deletes with an
  FPR bounded by the fingerprint width, not the load. Not for: removing untrusted /
  never-inserted keys, or duplicate-heavy streams (a key added > 2b times overflows its
  bucket pair), or the smallest static space (XOR / BinaryFuse).
- Quotient (decisions/0016..0017): ONE open-addressed LINEAR slot array. A key's 32-bit hash
  splits into a QUOTIENT (home slot index, high bits) and a REMAINDER (stored, low r bits);
  same-home keys form a RUN, adjacent runs a CLUSTER under linear probing, encoded by 3
  METADATA bits per slot (is_occupied bit0, is_continuation bit1, is_shifted bit2) packed in
  the low 3 bits of each byte-aligned word (remainder in the high bits: word=(remainder<<3)|
  metadata). A slot is EMPTY iff all 3 metadata bits are 0 (remainder 0 is a legal remainder).
  Query: !is_occupied(home) -> absent; else walk left to the cluster start, count occupied
  homes to find this home's run, scan the (sorted) run for r. It DELETES via a real
  remove(key) -> boolean (repairs metadata by REBUILDING the affected cluster through the
  insert path -- correct by construction), and ALSO ships merge() + resize() -- cold paths
  that reconstruct each element's identity from its stored (quotient,remainder) pair WITHOUT
  the original keys (the bit budget p=q0+r is fixed for the filter's lifetime), preserving
  membership (0 false negatives) + exact size. Remainder width r=ceil(log2(1/fpp)); the slot
  word is r+3 bits, byte-aligned to Uint8Array (r<=5) or Uint16Array (r 6..13); r+3>16
  (fpp<1/2^13 ~0.000122) throws at construction. Slot count 2^q >= ceil(capacity/0.90); q+r
  must fit one 32-bit hash. Stores MULTIPLICITY (does not dedup, like Cuckoo). FPR is
  remainder-quantized to load*2^-r (typically UNDER target -- r rounds up); fpp() reports
  that. Two honest fail-closed edges: (1) add at the 0.90 load ceiling (or whose linear
  cluster shift would run off the end) THROWS a [lite-filter] Error and is a byte-identical
  no-op (decisions/0016), never a silent drop; headroom via size vs capacity; (2) removing a
  NEVER-INSERTED key whose (quotient,remainder) collides with a real key removes that other
  key's fingerprint -> a false negative for it (decisions/0017) -- only remove keys you
  inserted. Space ~23 bits/item at fpp 0.01 (16-bit slot words + guard, metadata + shift
  overhead). Good for: membership + deletes when the filter must MERGE or GROW over its
  lifetime (the first family member that does either without the keys). Not for: removing
  untrusted keys, duplicate-heavy streams (multiplicity fills toward the ceiling), the
  tightest space (Bloom is lower), growing quotient entropy past q0 (resize adds headroom,
  not new quotient bits -- decisions/0016), or the smallest static space (XOR / Binary Fuse).
- XorFilter (decisions/0018..0020): the FIRST STATIC member -- built ONCE from a KNOWN key
  set via XorFilter.from(iterable, options) (or the .build alias), then FROZEN. It approaches
  the ~1.23x information-theoretic space lower bound by peeling a 3-uniform hypergraph: the
  fingerprint array is 3 equal SEGMENTS of length bl = ceil(1.23*n/3)+32 (total 3*bl ~=
  1.23*n+96 slots), each key touches one slot per segment, and slots are assigned in REVERSE
  peel order so a key's three slots XOR to its fingerprint. Query: fingerprint(key) ==
  fp[h0]^fp[h1]^fp[h2] -- zero allocation, no branch on build state. It DEDUPES its input
  (keys are a SET, not multiplicity -- contrast Cuckoo / Quotient); size == capacity ==
  |Set(keys)|. It is IMMUTABLE (decisions/0019): add / remove / clear and new XorFilter() all
  throw a [lite-filter] Error (rebuild with XorFilter.from(newKeys) to change membership).
  Fingerprint width fw = 8 when fpp >= 2^-8 (~0.0039), else 16; fpp < 2^-16 throws (the 16-bit
  floor, inclusive). Delivered FPR is the width-quantized 2^-fw, typically UNDER target (fpp()
  reports it): MEASURED ~0.0039 at fw=8, ~9.84 bits/item at n=1e6 -- LEANER than Cuckoo (~21) /
  Quotient (~23), competitive with Bloom (~9.6) at a lower FPR. Build is a cold path (peeling
  scaffold allocates); on a peel failure it RESEEDS deterministically (seed ^ attempt*
  0x9e3779b1) up to 100 times, then THROWS [lite-filter] -- NEVER a partial build (the
  fail-OPEN guard asserts the peel stack reached n before any fingerprint is assigned).
  Exhaustion is expected only for a DEGENERATE set (many keys that String()-encode
  identically -> duplicate edges no reseed can separate). Good for: a large, KNOWN, read-only
  key set where the smallest space at a given FPR matters (e.g. a shipped dictionary / URL
  blocklist). Not for: incremental adds, deletes, or a set that changes (use a mutable member).
- BinaryFuse (decisions/0022): the 7th and FINAL member -- STATIC like XOR (built ONCE via
  BinaryFuse.from(iterable, options) / .build, then FROZEN; add/remove/clear and new
  BinaryFuse() all throw), a construction-algorithm SWAP over XOR (Graf & Lemire, "Binary Fuse
  Filters: Fast and Smaller Than Xor Filters", 2022). It reuses the peel + reverse-assign
  substrate and the snapshot integrity checksum, but replaces XOR's 3 equal DISJOINT segments
  with 3 OVERLAPPING fuse segments selected by a multiply-shift (mulhiU32(h, scl) picks the
  first segment base in [0, scl); the next two are one/two segments further, perturbed
  within-segment), so it packs TIGHTER: ~1.13x slots/item (segLen = 2^floor(log(n)/log(3.33)
  +2.25) clamped, segCount from a ~1.125 load), ~9.04 bits/item at n=1e6 -- LEANER than XOR's
  ~9.85 -- and it builds FASTER. Same byte-aligned width door (fw 8/16, fpp < 2^-16 throws),
  same width-quantized 2^-fw FPR (MEASURED ~0.0039 at fw=8), same deterministic reseed x100
  then throw, same fail-OPEN peel-completeness guard, same dedupe (keys are a SET). restore()
  RE-DERIVES the segment geometry from the count (rejecting an internally-inconsistent sl/sc/
  fp.length triple) before the chk check. Good for: a static, KNOWN, read-only key set where you
  want the SMALLEST space and fastest build -- the default static choice. Not for: incremental
  adds, deletes, or a set that changes (use a mutable member).

## Construction

new Bloom(capacity, { fpp = 0.01, seed?, keys?: 'int', stats?: true })
new CountingBloom(capacity, { fpp = 0.01, seed?, keys?: 'int', stats?: true })
new BlockedBloom(capacity, { fpp = 0.01, seed?, keys?: 'int', stats?: true })
new Cuckoo(capacity, { fpp = 0.01, seed?, keys?: 'int', stats?: true })
new Quotient(capacity, { fpp = 0.01, seed?, keys?: 'int', stats?: true })
XorFilter.from(iterable, { fpp = 0.01, seed?, keys?: 'int', stats?: true })  // static; .build alias
BinaryFuse.from(iterable, { fpp = 0.01, seed?, keys?: 'int', stats?: true })  // static; .build alias

Sizing (decisions/0002): m = ceil(-n * ln(fpp) / ln(2)^2), k = round((m/n) * ln(2)),
k clamped to >= 1. All Bloom-family members share the sizing; CountingBloom stores
ceil(m/2) bytes (two 4-bit counters per byte) where Bloom stores ceil(m/32) 32-bit words;
BlockedBloom stores ceil(m/512)*16 words (nb 512-bit blocks) and clamps k to <= 512.
Cuckoo sizes differently (decisions/0014): fingerprint width f = ceil(log2(8/fpp))
byte-aligned to 8 or 16 bits, bucket count nb = pow2 >= ceil(capacity/(4*0.95)), store
nb*4 slots (Uint8Array or Uint16Array); real slot capacity is nb*4, headroom via size vs
capacity. Quotient sizes differently (decisions/0016): remainder width r = ceil(log2(1/fpp)),
slot word r+3 bits byte-aligned to 8 or 16 bits, slot count nslots = pow2 >= ceil(capacity/
0.90), plus GUARD spillover slots (max(1024, nslots>>3)); q+r must fit one 32-bit hash.
XorFilter sizes differently (decisions/0018): 3 segments of bl = ceil(1.23*n/3)+32 slots
(n = deduped key count), fingerprint fw = 8 or 16 bits byte-aligned, store 3*bl slots
(Uint8Array or Uint16Array); it takes the whole key set up front (no incremental capacity).
BinaryFuse sizes differently (decisions/0022): segLen sl = clamp(2^floor(log(n)/log(3.33)
+2.25), 4, 262144), segCount sc = max(1, ceil(round(n*sizeFactor)/sl) - 2) with sizeFactor =
max(1.125, 0.875+0.25*log(1e6)/log(n)), store (sc+2)*sl slots byte-aligned to fw; n=1 and n=2
land on the small-n clamp (sl=4, sc=1, 12 slots). Fail-closed doors: fpp not in (0,1),
capacity < 1, an overflowing store, (for Cuckoo) a fingerprint width > 16 bits, (for Quotient)
a slot word > 16 bits or a q+r budget > 32 bits, or (for XorFilter / BinaryFuse) an empty key
set, fpp < 2^-16, or 100 exhausted peel attempts all throw a [lite-filter] Error at
construction. null is not zero: an unsized filter is never a zero-capacity one.

## The honesty hook (the bench's whole point)

The textbook fpp = (1 - e^(-kn/m))^k assumes independent, uniform hash positions.
Under real key distributions, at high load factor / near-full fill, the MEASURED FPR
runs OVER the formula. Bench.mjs prints "% over theoretical" for four seeded
workloads (uniform, zipfian, sequential, adversarial near-full) checked against a
real Set oracle, so the divergence is the first thing you see. A number from a paper
is a hypothesis, not your filter's behavior on your keys -- MEASURE.

## Guarantees

- Zero allocation on add + mightContain (strict on keys:'int'; string keys too).
  Proven by node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs and the lite-perf-gate scenarios.
- No false negatives: 1e6 adds then requery = exactly 0 false negatives (torture).
- Bounded FPR: n=1e5, fpp=0.01, 1e6 disjoint probes -> measured FPR <= 0.0125
  (<= 25% over the formula), checked against a Set oracle (torture).
- CountingBloom deletes: add/mightContain/remove on keys:'int' are 0 scavenges at N
  and 8N (perf-gate); 1e5 mixed add/remove ops -> 0 false negatives for present keys
  and sum(nibbles) <= k*size (torture).
- BlockedBloom locality: add/mightContain on keys:'int' are 0 scavenges at N and 8N
  (perf-gate); every set bit of a key lies in ONE 512-bit block (validate); measured
  FPR within its honest ceiling (<= 0.0175) and PROVEN over plain-Bloom theory
  (> 0.00949) -- the locality penalty is visible, not hidden (torture, decisions/0013).
- Cuckoo deletes + fail-closed: add/mightContain/remove on keys:'int' are 0 scavenges at
  N and 8N (perf-gate; two-bucket b=4 scan, single scalar victim register on kicks, no
  scratch array); 1e6 adds -> 0 false negatives; bounded-keyspace add/remove churn -> 0
  false negatives for present keys and net size == present; measured FPR <= 0.0090
  (~0.0061, UNDER the configured 0.01 -- width quantization) with 0 false negatives; and a
  small over-filled filter PROVABLY THROWS after 500 kicks (fail-closed, torture,
  decisions/0014). nonzero-slot count == size (validate).
- Quotient deletes + merges + resizes + fail-closed: add/mightContain/remove on keys:'int'
  are 0 scavenges at N and 8N (perf-gate; linear-probe split + shift, preallocated cluster
  scratch on remove); 1e6 adds -> 0 false negatives; bounded-keyspace add/remove churn -> 0
  false negatives for present keys and net size == present; measured FPR <= 0.0090 (~0.0060,
  UNDER the configured 0.01 -- remainder quantization) with 0 false negatives; resize (grow +
  shrink) and disjoint merge round-trips -> 0 false negatives + preserved/additive size; a
  small over-filled filter PROVABLY THROWS at the 0.90 load ceiling and a thrown add is a
  byte-identical no-op (torture, decisions/0016). metadata-set-slot count == size and
  per-cluster #homes == #runs after churn (validateQuotient -- the shift-back repair proof).
- XorFilter static + space-optimal + fail-closed: mightContain on keys:'int' is 0 scavenges
  at N=200000 and 8N=1600000 (perf-gate; 3 hashes, 3 modulo reductions, an XOR-compare, no
  scratch); a filter built from 1e6 distinct keys reads back with EXACTLY 0 false negatives
  (which can hold ONLY if the peel was complete -- the fail-OPEN regression gate); n=1e5,
  fpp=0.01 (fw=8) over 1e6 disjoint probes -> measured FPR <= 0.0050 (~0.0039, UNDER the
  configured 0.01 -- width quantization) AND > 0 (non-vacuous); a DEGENERATE set exhausts 100
  reseeds and THROWS [lite-filter]; add/remove/clear/new all THROW [lite-filter]; 50
  build-then-drop cycles leave the leak tracker at 0 (torture, decisions/0018..0020).
  fp.length == 3*bl and bl == ceil(1.23*count/3)+32 (validateXor).
- BinaryFuse static + SMALLEST + fail-closed: mightContain on keys:'int' is 0 scavenges at
  N=200000 and 8N=1600000 (perf-gate; 3 hashes, a multiply-shift + 2 within-segment offsets,
  an XOR-compare, no scratch); a filter built from 1e6 distinct keys reads back with EXACTLY 0
  false negatives (the fail-OPEN regression gate); measured slots/item 1.1305 (in [1.08,1.13], 2dp)
  and bits/item 9.04 <= 9.30 at n=1e6 -- LEANER than XOR's ~9.85; n=1e5, fpp=0.01 (fw=8) over
  1e6 disjoint probes -> measured FPR <= 0.0050 (~0.0038, UNDER target) AND > 0 (non-vacuous);
  a DEGENERATE set exhausts 100 reseeds and THROWS; add/remove/clear/new all THROW; restore()
  rejects an internally-inconsistent segment geometry (re-derived from count) and a chk flip;
  50 build-then-drop cycles leave the leak tracker at 0 (torture, decisions/0022). geometry ==
  _bfDims(count) and fp.length == (sc+2)*sl (validateBinaryFuse).
- Fail closed on every unverified state; [lite-filter]-tagged errors throughout.

## Testing

node:test only. npm test (boundary suite), npm run test:types (tsc surface gate),
npm run torture (leak + GC gate + differential oracle), npm run torture:controls
(the must-fail proof), npm run test:perf (lite-perf-gate zero-alloc scenarios),
npm run bench (the measurement tool), npm run verify (all of the gates).

## What this is not

Not a cryptographic structure (fingerprints are not MACs). Not an exact set (that is
what Set is for). Not a key-value store (it stores membership, never values).
